sections.text: 1 In catalogo supra scripto vocatur ὁ ἀπὸ τῆς εὐδαίμονος Ἀραβίας (I, p. 84, l. 8). — Alius liber eiusdem catalogi, scilicet l. 6 : Ἡ βίβλος τοῦ περὶ ἐμπορίας, sic citatur in principo cap. ξςʹ Apomasaris [f. 51v] : Ἀνέγνων ἐν τῷ (sic) ἐμπειρικοῖς βίβλοις· ὅτι εἰ βούλει γνῶναι τὴν ὥραν κ. τ. λ. Legendum est igitur περὶ ἐμπειρίας. 2 In libro Hermetis τῶν μυστηρίων, ut videtur, qui in catalogo Apomasaris commemoratur (I, p. 84, 14).
sections.en: 1 In the catalog written above he is called ὁ ἀπὸ τῆς εὐδαίμονος Ἀραβίας ('the one from Arabia Felix') (I, p. 84, l. 8). — Another book of the same catalog, namely l. 6: Ἡ βίβλος τοῦ περὶ ἐμπορίας ('The book of the one concerning trade'), is cited thus in the beginning of chapter 66 of Apomasar [f. 51v]: Ἀνέγνων ἐν τῷ (sic) ἐμπειρικοῖς βίβλοις· ὅτι εἰ βούλει γνῶναι τὴν ὥραν κ. τ. λ. ('I read in the empirical books: that if you wish to know the hour etc.'). It must be read therefore περὶ ἐμπειρίας ('concerning experience'). 2 In the book of Hermes τῶν μυστηρίων ('of the mysteries'), as it seems, which is commemorated in the catalog of Apomasar (I, p. 84, 14).

summary.headline: Apomasar on Marriage Lots and Stellar Agency
summary.text: Apomasar discusses ancient and recent Arabian astrologers and the methods of the kings of Arabia Felix, then gives a horoscopic test using lots derived from Jupiter, Venus, and Mars to determine whether a woman is a legitimate wife or companion. A further passage from Hermes Trismegistus argues that stars are not independently active, using Jupiter as an instructional example.
